question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Sarah / will singing / at the concert / on Saturday.
options: will singing
at the concert
Sarah
on Saturday
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "will singing"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "will singing" is incorrect because after the modal verb "will", we must use the base form (V1) of the verb, not the present participle (V1+ing).
☛ "Will" is a modal auxiliary verb used to indicate future tense, and it always takes the first form of the verb (sing).
☛ The correct sentence should be: "Sarah will sing at the concert on Saturday."
☛ Here, "singing" is incorrect because it suggests a continuous tense, whereas "will" requires the simple future tense.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Modal verbs (will, shall, can, may, must, etc.) are always followed by the base form (V1) of the verb.
☛ The future simple tense follows the structure: "will/shall + V1".
☛ The present participle (V1+ing) is used in continuous tenses, such as: is singing, was singing, will be singing.

Example:
InCorrect - He will eating dinner.
Correct - He will eat dinner.

☛ Adverbs of frequency (hardly, never) are not modified by 'very.'

Example:

Correct - He runs very fast.

question:

Solution: Correct Answer is "good"


Explanation:

☛ "Best" (superlative degree) is used when comparing three or more persons/things.
☛ "More good" and "goodest" are grammatically incorrect because "good" already has fixed comparative and superlative forms: "better" and "best".


Grammar Rules:
☛ Adjectives have three degrees: Positive, Comparative, Superlative.
☛ Positive degree describes a quality of a person or thing (e.g., good, tall, beautiful).
☛ Comparative degree compares two persons or things (e.g., better, taller, more beautiful).
☛ Superlative degree compares three or more persons/things to show the highest degree (e.g., best, tallest, most beautiful).
☛ Some adjectives have irregular comparative and superlative forms, e.g., good → better → best.


Example:
InCorrect - Pankaj is a better cook.
Correct - Pankaj is a good cook.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Past Continuous Tense describes actions in progress at a specific past time. Formula: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing.
☛ Passive Voice is used when the subject receives the action. Structure: Object + was/were + V3.
☛ While vs. When: "While" pairs with continuous actions, "When" with sudden/short actions.

Example:

Correct - While she was watching the movie...
